clue.text: Decoration and high honour presented after pageantry

blocks.note: pomp is splendid ceremonial display
the OM is the Order of Merit, a top British honour

explanation.surface: An award ceremony where a top honour is handed out after much pomp and display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presented after' puts the honour second, behind the pageantry. The Order of Merit is a select award given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a woolly ball used as an ornamental trim on hats and costumes.

clue.text: Hold forth in elaborate style, concealing name

indicators.note: concealing something puts it out of sight, so that letter disappears from the word

blocks.note: an elaborate style is ornate
N is the standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone speechifying in a flowery manner while keeping a name secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N from ORNATE. The letters also sit inside 'elaborate', a bonus for the solver who spots it.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to give a pompous speech, which is what holding forth means as an idiom.

clue.text: Worst and best hiatus in race?

blocks.note: the pits is slang for the very worst
top means best, first-rate

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about the highs and lows of a pause during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a playful description rather than a dictionary one.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing a car briefly halts in the pits for fuel or tyres, a short break mid-race.

clue.text: Damage horse, having tail docked

indicators.note: docking a tail cuts off its end, so the last letter of the word goes

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: Harm done to a horse whose tail has been cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Docking really is done to horses' tails, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or impair it, a direct synonym of damaging it.

clue.text: Religious group — or part

blocks.note: a sect is a religious group
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reads like a dictionary choice: a religious body, or else a portion.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and 'or' make it look like two alternative meanings, but 'or' is simply part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct section or division of a whole, such as an economy or area.

clue.text: Small chappies moving about in rocket?

indicators.note: things moving about change their places, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Little fellows bustling around inside a rocket, like tiny astronauts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a rocket is only an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is one kind of craft built to travel beyond the atmosphere, hence a definition by example.

clue.text: Restrict piano study first

blocks.note: to cram is to study intensively
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Limit piano practice by making the student study other things first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study first' tells you the study word comes before the piano letter, though the clue names piano first.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to hinder or confine, as in cramping someone's style.

clue.text: Folding business that keeps producing figures?

definitions.text: Folding business that keeps producing figures?

blocks.clueFragment: Folding business that keeps producing figures?
blocks.note: surface reading: a company that goes bust yet keeps issuing accounts

blocks.clueFragment: Folding business that keeps producing figures?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the craft of creasing paper repeatedly into shapes of animals and birds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Folding' suggests a firm collapsing and 'figures' suggests accounts; both really refer to paper creased into models.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese paper craft is entirely about folding sheets to make figures such as cranes.

clue.text: Bugs one appearing in dodgy cabaret

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or not right, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: Germs turning up in a seedy nightclub show.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra letter joins the club word before everything is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs is informal for germs, microbes that cause illness, which is what these organisms are.

clue.text: Return of opera-singer making you keen

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: A favourite soprano's comeback makes you an eager fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic, a straightforward synonym for keen.

clue.text: Satisfied to accommodate a carnivore's food

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in and house, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: needs that are satisfied are met
taken as written

explanation.surface: Content to make room for what a carnivore eats.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnivores live on animal flesh, which is what this food is.

clue.text: The turn is interrupted by a performer

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle

blocks.note: taken as written
a spin is a turn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stage act cut short by an actor barging in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The turn' sounds like a variety act; here only the second word is broken into.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, from Thespis, traditionally the first actor of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Roughly 66 per cent ultimately get this word wrong

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept
words put wrong are out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the end of this word
these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-referential complaint that most people end up misspelling a particular word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' looks like it goes with 'per cent', but it picks the last letter of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two thirds is 66.67 per cent, so roughly 66 per cent is a fair approximation of the fraction.

clue.text: Computer program in expo curtailed name of old poet

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is lost
one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: an expo is an exhibition or show
an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: Software at a trade fair named after an ancient poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Trim the show word to three letters, then put the program inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the Greek lyric poet of Lesbos, writing around 600 BC.

clue.text: Source of irritation largely dissipated

indicators.note: something dissipated is scattered, so the letters are dispersed and regrouped

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: An annoyance that has mostly gone away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' looks like it modifies 'dissipated', but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy causes itching, sneezing and rashes, so it is a cause of bodily irritation.

clue.text: Over-confidence? Core feature with endless peril

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is chopped off

blocks.note: a hub is the central part of something
risk is danger, peril

explanation.surface: Asks whether cockiness lies at the heart of reckless danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is excessive pride or arrogance, the overweening self-belief of Greek tragedy.

clue.text: Favour penning a couple of lines for part of cartoon

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so one part goes inside another

blocks.note: a boon is a favour
taken as written
L is short for line, so two of them

explanation.surface: A cartoonist doing a favour by drawing a few strokes for a strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' and 'lines' suggest drawing or writing, which suits the cartoon surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In comics, speech or thought bubbles coming from characters are known by this inflatable name.

clue.text: Leading vessel sinks with it

blocks.note: to flag is to tire or droop, to sink
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A lead ship going down and taking everything with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinks' fits a ship too well; here it means weakens.
explanation.definitionFit: The flagship carries the admiral's flag and leads a fleet, so it is the chief ship.

clue.text: Good American fan of Grand Theft Auto?

blocks.note: G is short for good
Amer. is an abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A decent American who enjoys a notorious crime video game.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand Theft Auto is a best-selling video game series, so a fan of it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamer plays video games, and the named game is one popular example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Large buffoon to stand idly by

blocks.note: L is short for large, as on clothing labels
an oaf is a clumsy fool

explanation.surface: A big clown who just stands around doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer looks like a noun for bread, but the definition is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to loaf is to idle or lounge about, doing nothing useful.

clue.text: Father picked up paintings, say, in different places

indicators.note: in a down clue, being picked up lifts a word so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
paintings are an example of art

explanation.surface: Dad collected pictures from all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' might suggest a sound-alike, but in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set apart are separated, located at a distance from each other.

clue.text: Stern former ruler I am to follow

blocks.note: GR, George Rex, is the cipher of past King Georges
the contraction I'm

explanation.surface: A severe ex-monarch announcing he will be next in line.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim means forbidding and severe in manner, close in sense to a stern look.

clue.text: Sensible to restrict access to a lot of beer

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: rationing restricts how much people may have
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A wise policy is limiting how much beer drinkers can get.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means reasonable and logical, governed by good sense.

clue.text: Metal temperature at home

blocks.note: T is short for temperature
in means at home

explanation.surface: How warm a metal is when kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin is a soft silvery element, chemical symbol Sn, one of the common metals.

clue.text: Extreme examples of curry powder, given to us for island state

indicators.note: extremes are the ends, so only the first and last letters of each word are kept

blocks.note: the two ends of this word
the two ends of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spice handed to us as the national dish of a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an independent republic occupying an island in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Total of ten baseball teams I catch in US city

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it

blocks.note: NY is New York
taken as written
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Ten ball clubs playing in an American city, with someone snaring a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: A baseball team fields nine players, so ten teams have that many in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine players per side multiplied by ten sides makes this number, a playful arithmetical definition.
